title: OpenTelemetry GenAI — Tracing Tool Calls End-to-End

questions.question: An agent is intermittently slow, and logs show only the LLM request. What observability structure helps locate a slow tool-server round-trip?
options: One unstructured final-answer log with no timing fields
One trace with parent-linked spans for agent, model, and tools
Separate unrelated trace ids for each step in a run
A prompt transcript that omits server-side operations
questions.explanation: One trace id groups the agent, LLM, tool, and MCP spans; parentSpanId records their nested path, so each duration can be followed through the run. Separate trace ids would hide how a slow server call relates to the reported agent delay.

questions.question: Which span kind fits an agent's own loop step rather than a call crossing a process boundary?
options: SERVER
INTERNAL
PRODUCER
CLIENT
questions.explanation: Use INTERNAL for work performed inside the agent process, such as its loop step. CLIENT marks an outbound call crossing a process boundary, such as a request to an LLM provider or MCP server; SERVER is the receiving side.

questions.question: Which pair of attributes identifies a specific tool call in a GenAI tool span?
options: gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.response.model
gen_ai.agent.name and gen_ai.agent.description
gen_ai.tool.name and gen_ai.tool.call.id
gen_ai.provider.name and gen_ai.request.model
questions.explanation: `gen_ai.tool.name` identifies the executor and `gen_ai.tool.call.id` identifies this particular invocation. Provider and model attributes identify the LLM backend, not which tool call ran or which same-tool request it represents.

questions.question: How can a parent and child span remain part of the same distributed trace?
options: Copy the prompt into each span name
Use the tool call id as the trace id for every run
Share the trace id and set the child's parentSpanId
Generate a new trace id for every child operation
questions.explanation: Spans share the trace id, and each child sets parentSpanId to its parent span id; that preserves both run membership and ancestry. Generating a new trace for a child splits it from the parent run and breaks end-to-end timing.

questions.question: Prompts and completions may contain sensitive content. What is the lesson's default capture policy?
options: Keep content capture off unless deliberately enabled
Store prompts only when the trace has no tool calls
Record every prompt in every span by default
Replace span attributes with full conversation text
questions.explanation: Keep prompt and completion content capture off by default because it can contain PII and large payloads; enable it only after review. Recording every prompt by default creates the privacy exposure the opt-in policy is designed to avoid.

questions.question: An MCP server uses stdio, which does not carry HTTP headers natively. How can the lesson propagate trace context?
options: Create a new trace at the server and discard the parent
Include traceparent manually in each request's _meta
Put the trace id only into the tool's display name
Wait for stdio to add an HTTP header automatically
questions.explanation: Stdio has no HTTP header channel, so put the W3C traceparent value into each request’s `_meta` for the server to log. Starting a new server trace discards the parent context, while waiting for an HTTP header on stdio cannot work.
